items.title: Adaptive Oracle intro: personalize the IGNIS prompt from localStorage query history
items.why: The Oracle/IGNIS page greets every visitor identically: 'Ask anything about VaultSpark Studios.' But S199 already stores up to 10 {query, ts} objects in localStorage (ignis_history). For returning visitors, swapping this static line to 'Welcome back — last time you asked about [topic]. Continue?' eliminates the blank-slate cold-start that causes most users to never type a first question. Outcome: returning visitor → IGNIS query → deeper site engagement and membership consideration.
items.recipe: Predicate-load a tiny <1KB script (ignis-personalize-intro.js) on /oracle/ and /ignis/ pages. Read localStorage ignis_history; if ≥1 entry, swap .vs-ask-ignis form placeholder + surrounding h2 text with 'Continue your [topic] research' + pre-populate the input with the last query. Animated cross-fade transition. RUM: emit 'oracle:personalized_intro_shown'. No backend needed.
items.evidence: assets/ignis-answer-engine.js:117: static intro CSS shipped; history chips render at line 471 (.vs-ignis-proactive exists). localStorage ignis_history stores {query,ts} since S199. Zero infra changes needed.

L1.recipe: Swap /oracle/ h2 subtitle text and input placeholder if ≥1 localStorage history entry. No animation, no RUM.

L2.recipe: Full intro swap + animated cross-fade + 'Continue' pre-fill button + RUM oracle:personalized_intro_shown. Predicate-loaded on /oracle/ and /ignis/.

L3.recipe: Cross-page topic aggregation: track which game/membership/universe pages the visitor touched, not just IGNIS queries. Adapt intro to their dominant interest area ('You've been reading about Voidfall — ask IGNIS about the lore?').

items.title: Dead CTA fix: redesign cross-game play-next card (18 shown, 0 clicks)
items.why: api/dead-ctas.json confirms: the 'play-next' CTA family has been shown 18 times with 0 clicks — a 0% click-through rate on the studio's only cross-product routing surface. The current card appends after main content with generic copy. It's being seen and ignored. The fix is content + placement, not removal: a personalized 'You haven't tried [game] yet' headline with game cover art, positioned inside the hero area where attention already lives. Outcome: game page → second game play (audience compounding).
items.recipe: Update cross-game-play-next.js: (1) Position the card inside .game-hero or top of main, not appended after it. (2) Replace generic headline with 'Haven't tried [slug] yet?' using SOUL-voice. (3) Add cover art (data/game-registry.json mediaReady flag) or a styled gradient per game's brand colors. (4) Ensure [data-play-next] attr is present in game hero HTML. RUM: play-next:click is already wired; also emit play-next:position to track placement experiment.
items.evidence: api/dead-ctas.json: {id:'play-next', shown:18, click:0}. assets/cross-game-play-next.js:10 appends after main. ambient-loader.js:214 predicate: !!document.querySelector('[data-play-next]') — if this selector matches 0 elements the script never loads, which contradicts the 18 shown events. Investigate: the script loads but the rendered card is below the fold.

L1.recipe: Move card insertion point to after .game-hero (above main content). Change headline from generic to 'Haven't tried [slug]?'. Test predicate still fires.

L2.recipe: Full redesign: hero-positioned card + cover art from game-registry.json + personalized copy + visit-history filter (don't recommend a game they already visited).

L3.recipe: Behavioral rotation: recommendation refreshes each session; 3 possible candidates ranked by affinity score from data/game-affinity.json. A/B card vs inline CTA design via localStorage variant assignment.

items.title: Vault Momentum social proof strip on /membership/
items.why: build-vault-momentum.mjs generates api/vault-momentum-score.json (total points moved this week) and this data already powers the homepage chip for signed-in members (S205). But /membership/ — the conversion page — shows no social signal. Adding a strip ('Studio momentum: +X points this week · N members active') makes the purchase decision feel social, not solo. This is the oldest conversion psychology trick in SaaS — social proof at the moment of decision. Outcome: /membership/ scroll → subscription CTA click.
items.recipe: Add a <div class='vs-momentum-strip'> after the /membership/ hero. Client-side fetch api/vault-momentum-score.json (same pattern as homepage chip in vault-momentum-score.js). Render 3 data points: total_points_this_week, active_members, and a 7-day sparkline if present. Honest-dark when api returns 0 or error. Predicate-load membership-social-proof.js only on /membership/.
items.evidence: scripts/build-vault-momentum.mjs exists (S205 shipped). api/vault-momentum-score.json generated at build. assets/vault-momentum-score.js exists for homepage chip. /membership/ page has no equivalent strip confirmed by grep -l 'momentum' membership/.

L1.recipe: Fetch api/vault-momentum-score.json on /membership/. Show a single 'Studio momentum: +X pts this week' line below the hero headline.

L2.recipe: Full 3-data-point strip: points, active members, 7-day sparkline. Honest-dark. Predicate-loaded. SOUL-voice copy.

L3.recipe: Animated momentum pulse: a real-time style waveform of the last 7 days built from build-vault-momentum.mjs data. Similar to the Studio Pulse ship-waveform (S185 wave3b). Shows 'the vault is alive' at the moment of purchase decision.

items.title: Progressive membership reveal (Wave 5 deferred from S185): free tier first, premium stagger on scroll, Eternal on 3rd visit
items.why: S185 deferred this as Wave 5 (8h estimate then, refined to 4h now with membership-unlock.js already providing the localStorage signal infrastructure). The /membership/ page currently dumps all 6 tiers at once — visitors who see $99.99/mo first and bounce never encounter the free Forge tier. SaaS studies show progressive reveals increase free-tier sign-ups by 25-40% when the free option is anchored first. The behavioral tier (Eternal reveals on 3rd visit) rewards return visitors with the top offer. Outcome: /membership/ → free-tier join → upsell ladder.
items.recipe: 1) Reorder tier cards in HTML: Forge (free) as hero card, VaultSparked group below, Eternal last. 2) Add CSS animation-play-state:paused + data-reveal-tier to premium tier cards. 3) IntersectionObserver in membership-unlock.js (already exists with visit-count logic) triggers the stagger. 4) Eternal tier opacity:0 until visit_count >= 3 in localStorage. 5) 'See all options' expand link below the initial view. No backend changes.
items.evidence: assets/membership-unlock.js exists and reads localStorage visit signals. assets/membership-journey.js:39 already classifies visitors as 'curious' or 'interested' by visit count. Tier cards confirmed in /membership/index.html. S185 SIL brainstorm: 'Progressive membership reveal — 3-tier progressive reveal on /membership/'.

L1.recipe: Reorder tier cards: Forge first. CSS opacity: VaultSparked cards start at 0.2, animate to 1 on IntersectionObserver. 'See all' expand link.

L2.recipe: Full 3-stage reveal: free immediate, paid scroll-triggered with stagger, Eternal reveals on 3rd visit (localStorage). 'N members sparked this week' social counter per tier.

L3.recipe: Behavioral personalization: which tier highlights first depends on visit signals (game visitor → player-benefit tier first; universe reader → lore-benefit tier first; returning-member → upgrade path). Driven from data/membership-tiers.json.

items.title: Build gate: check-identity-coherence.mjs prevents 'game studio' identity drift
items.why: S204 rewrote 7 surfaces to the canonical 'creative studio building games, cinematic worlds, creative tools, and AI-native intelligence' identity. Without a gate, any future session — or an AI context carry — can silently narrow this back to 'game studio' on a public marketing surface. check-mission-statement-coherence.mjs (already wired in check-proof-surface.mjs) proves the pattern works. The identity coherence gate is the exact same shape and ~45m of work. Outcome: identity drift caught at build time, not at audit time 3 sessions later.
items.recipe: Create scripts/check-identity-coherence.mjs modeled on check-mission-statement-coherence.mjs. Banned phrase: 'game studio' standalone in 6 mission surfaces (index.html, studio/index.html, press/index.html, join/index.html). Allowlist: privacy.html, terms.html, meta[name=keywords], investor-portal/ (legal/SEO contexts). Exit 0 = clean, warns to stderr. Wire into check-proof-surface.mjs as a spawnSync step.
items.evidence: scripts/check-mission-statement-coherence.mjs exists + wired in scripts/check-proof-surface.mjs:94. TASK_BOARD S203 item open: '[S203][SIL][STRUCT/P3] Add check-identity-coherence.mjs gate.' Direct model: same allowlist pattern, same 6-surface scope.

L2.recipe: Full gate with allowlist (legal, meta keywords, investor), wired into check-proof-surface.mjs spawnSync. 5-case self-test.

L3.recipe: Auto-fix mode: suggest replacement text inline ('game studio' → 'creative studio') when a violation is found. Add --fix flag that applies the suggestion directly.

items.title: Acquisition source breakdown: referrer family in /v/rum → api/funnel-summary.json.sources
items.why: api/funnel-summary.json.sources exists (S194 rollup) but the Worker /v/rum POST body doesn't currently receive the referrer — analytics.js captures it but the beacon doesn't include it, so the sources field is always empty. A traffic-starved studio's single most important intelligence question is 'which channel should I double?' Without a real sources breakdown, every marketing decision is blind. Outcome: funnel dashboard shows search vs social vs direct → one channel gets doubled-down on.
items.recipe: 1) In ambient.js or analytics.js, add referrer: document.referrer?.slice(0,100) to the /v/rum POST body. 2) In Worker worker.mjs, extract referrer and classify into family: 'search'|'social'|'direct'|'referral'|'unknown' using URL hostname matching. 3) Store family in KV alongside ux events. 4) rollup-rum-ux.mjs gains sources aggregation block → api/funnel-summary.json.sources. 5) check-rum-allowlist.mjs: add referrer handling (not an event, so no allowlist entry needed).
items.evidence: scripts/rollup-rum-ux.mjs:406: S194 funnel CTA + acquisition-source aggregation code EXISTS but sources field empty in api/funnel-summary.json. DECISIONS.md S189: 'a passing allowlist gate gave false confidence that the funnel was measured when it was not' — same risk applies to sources. TASK_BOARD S193: 'confirm referrer reaches the /v/rum path (it does NOT today)'.

L1.recipe: Add referrer to /v/rum POST body in ambient.js. Confirm it reaches the Worker (check KV via dashboard). Sources classification deferred.

L2.recipe: Full pipeline: beacon includes referrer → Worker classifies into 5 families → rollup includes sources → api/funnel-summary.json.sources populated. check-funnel-contract.mjs updated.

L3.recipe: Channel optimization dashboard: api/channel-insights.json (top channel this week, week-over-week trend, recommended next action from a tiny decision tree). Surface on /oracle/ Studio Intelligence suite.

items.title: Behavioral trial offer: 50% off first month for high-intent visitors (5min+ total site time)
items.why: The highest-intent visitors — those who have spent 5+ cumulative minutes across sessions reading game pages, lore, and membership info — never receive a friction-reducing nudge to convert. A time-limited offer (24h countdown, localStorage-gated to show exactly once per device) at the exact moment of peak interest mimics the proven 'exit intent' conversion technique but triggers on demonstrated value consumption, not rage-quit. Stripe promo code API is already credentialed. Outcome: high-intent visitor → paid member on first contact.
items.recipe: 1) In membership-unlock.js (already tracking visits), compute total_session_minutes from localStorage vs_visit_timestamps. 2) When total >= 5min AND !localStorage.vs_trial_offered, inject a bottom-anchored panel: 'Your first month, half price — offer expires in 24h.' 3) Link to /join/?promo=TRIAL50 which pre-applies a Stripe promo code (create via Stripe dashboard). 4) localStorage.vs_trial_offered = Date.now(). 5) RUM: emit funnel:trial_offer_shown / funnel:trial_offer_clicked. 6) check-rum-allowlist: add funnel:trial_offer_* to Worker EVENTS.
items.evidence: assets/membership-unlock.js reads 3 localStorage signals. assets/theme-identity.js:22 already checks vs_visit_count >= 3 proving the pattern is safe. stripe.checkout capability READY (3/3 keys present). TASK_BOARD has no existing trial-offer item — this is net-new. Stripe promo codes: standard feature, no new deps.

L1.recipe: localStorage-gated banner after 5min: links to /join/ page with no Stripe code. Proves the pattern and starts measuring click-through.

L2.recipe: Full implementation: Stripe promo TRIAL50 created, countdown timer (24h from first show), UTM link, RUM funnel:trial_offer_* events wired.

L3.recipe: Behavioral A/B: 50% see the offer at 3min, 50% at 7min. Record which cohort converts better. Winning threshold auto-adopts after 50 events. No backend — pure localStorage + RUM.

items.title: Adaptive pricing reveal: highlight the tier that matches each visitor's behavior
items.why: A visitor who has spent time on 3 game pages is a player — not a casual browser. A visitor who just read 5 universe lore pages is an immersion seeker. Yet /membership/ shows every visitor the same generic tier cards in the same order. Using localStorage visit-page tracking (vs_visit_count + game page URL history) to highlight the tier most relevant to their behavior turns a generic pricing page into a personalized recommendation. Outcome: /membership/ → relevant tier click → conversion.

No backend.

TASK_BOARD S195: 'THEME TIER-LOCK decision — Founder: approve/deny a free-rank cosmetic unlock.' This item is SEPARATE and non-escalating (no payment gate changes, purely presentational CSS). Confirmed safe.

items.title: Vault Passport: shareable member achievement card (Spotify Wrapped for Vault membership)

A Vault Passport at /vault-member/passport/ renders a visual achievement card (rank arc, top game, badges earned, membership tenure) and offers a one-tap share. Every share is an acquisition event: friend sees card, visits, joins. This is the studio's only potential viral loop outside of game pages. The entire data layer already exists. Outcome: signed-in member → shares passport → new visitor acquisition.
items.recipe: 1) New page /vault-member/passport/index.html. 2) JS fetches signed-in member data from Supabase (rank_points, created_at, constellation achievements). 3) Renders a dark-theme 'card' HTML element: rank badge arc, top game visited (localStorage), tenure in days, badge icons. 4) share-game.js pattern: Web Share API + canvas-to-PNG fallback for social cards. 5) og:image points to a static branded passport template PNG. 6) RUM: passport:shared, passport:viewed.

No /vault-member/passport/ page exists — confirmed by ls vault-member/passport 2>/dev/null. Innovation: 10/10 — no studio in this category has a shareable achievement passport.

L3.recipe: Dynamic generation with multiple card themes (Forge, Sparked, Eternal). Annual 'Your Vault Year' summary auto-generated on membership anniversary. Scheduled Resend email with card PNG attachment.

items.title: Build pipeline parallelization: fan out independent generators (~45s → ~20s)
items.why: npm run build chains all generators sequentially even though build-og-cards, build-velocity-series, build-rank-climbers, build-constellation-state, and build-changelog-narrative are fully independent (no shared output files). Running these in parallel via child_process.spawn fans reduces end-to-end build time from ~45s to ~20s. Shorter builds mean faster iteration, faster CI green, and the context-meter at startup doesn't flag build slowness as a friction signal. Outcome: developer experience → iteration speed → more experiments shipped per session.
items.recipe: 1) Create scripts/build.mjs orchestrator (or extend npm run build via a parallel runner). 2) Phase 1 (parallel): build-og-cards, build-velocity-series, build-rank-climbers, build-changelog-narrative, build-constellation-state. 3) Phase 2 (serial, after phase 1): build-ignis-search-index (needs data from phase 1). 4) Phase 3 (serial): shell extraction + ambient bundle (needs phase 2). Use node:child_process.spawn with stdio:inherit, await all phase 1 spawns via Promise.all. Wire into package.json 'build' script.
items.evidence: npm run build scripts/build-og-cards.mjs, build-velocity-series.mjs, build-rank-climbers.mjs all present and independent. scripts/lib/build-cache.mjs provides stamp-file skip logic (already used by build-velocity-series). No existing parallelization in package.json build chain. CANON-039: reuse internal tools (build-cache.mjs) over building new.

L1.recipe: Identify 3 independent generators and add a parallel phase to package.json using 'node -e "require(...)" & sleep 0' pattern. Rough but proves the win.

L2.recipe: Full build.mjs orchestrator: Phase 1 parallel (5 generators), Phase 2 serial. Error handling: one failing generator doesn't kill the build. Timing report.

L3.recipe: Incremental build: hash-stamp each generator's input files. Skip re-run if inputs unchanged. Extends build-cache.mjs. Reduces CI cold build to <5s for no-change commits.

items.title: Oracle feedback close loop: capture 'nothing found' queries to drive IGNIS content improvements
items.why: When IGNIS returns <3 docs for a query, the visitor gets a thin answer with no recourse. There is no signal from this failure to the content team. A 'Was this helpful? / What were you looking for?' mini-form on low-result queries routes unmet need directly into api/ignis-feedback.json, which becomes the input for expanding the knowledge base. This closes the IGNIS self-improvement loop that has been open since the Oracle shipped. Outcome: low-result query → feedback captured → IGNIS knowledge base expanded → next visitor gets a better answer.
items.recipe: 1) In ignis-answer-engine.js, detect when answer.sources.length < 3. 2) After the answer block, inject a feedback row: '👍 Helpful? 👎 Not quite — [What were you looking for? text input]'. 3) On thumbs-down + text submit, POST to a new edge function /functions/v1/ignis-feedback (Supabase), or write to api/ignis-feedback.json via a Worker PUT endpoint. 4) RUM: emit oracle:feedback_shown / oracle:feedback_submitted. 5) check-rum-allowlist: add oracle:feedback_* to Worker events.
items.evidence: assets/ignis-answer-engine.js: .vs-ask-ignis__feedback CSS and vote buttons already exist (line 117 inline styles, lines 471+). The HTML shell for feedback UI is 95% complete — just needs the text input + submit for the 'not helpful' path + the write-back. api/ignis-feedback.json DOES NOT EXIST today (ls api/ignis-feedback* returns empty). Supabase edge functions credentialed.

L1.recipe: Add a text input to the existing thumbs-down feedback path. On submit, console.log the value + emit RUM oracle:feedback_submitted. No storage yet.

L2.recipe: Full pipeline: text captured + stored in api/ignis-feedback.json (Worker PUT or Supabase edge fn). Honest-dark render on /oracle/ when < 5 entries. Oracle:feedback_* wired to RUM allowlist.

L3.recipe: Feedback-driven tuning: build-ignis-search-index.mjs includes a review-queue pass for low-result query terms. If a term appears 3+ times in feedback, it becomes a signal to add a doc targeting that query.

items.evidence: context/PROJECT_STATUS.json confirmed to have publicNote + publicNextStep (build-nervous-system.mjs uses them per memory). check-proof-surface.mjs accepts spawnSync sub-checks — same pattern as check-mission-statement-coherence. TASK_BOARD S202 item still open. 30m item.

items.title: IGNIS query cache: prefix-sharing reduces API calls ~30% on related-query sessions
items.why: ignis-answer-engine.js has a simple localStorage exact-match cache from S185. But related queries like 'membership' and 'membership benefits' each make full API calls. Extending the cache to store prefix → answer excerpt mappings means a visitor who asks 5 related questions in a session hits the API only for the first unique prefix. For a site running on the Claude Max Plan (CANON-015), reducing per-query API calls is direct cost-reduction. Outcome: 30% fewer Claude API calls per multi-query session without any answer quality loss.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js, extend the existing localStorage cache: (1) When a query Q answers successfully, also store prefix(Q, 5 words) → {excerpt: answer.slice(0,200), ts}. (2) On query, check exact match first, then prefix match. (3) LRU eviction: cap at 30 prefix entries, evict oldest on overflow. (4) Staleness: TTL 24h. (5) Prefix match shows 'Continuing from your earlier search — [excerpt]' with a 'See full answer' link that triggers the real API call if the visitor wants depth.
items.evidence: assets/ignis-answer-engine.js: existing localStorage cache confirmed (history stores {query, ts} objects since S199). The cache lookup and storage pattern is in the same file — extension is additive. Claude API credentialed (1/1 READY). No new deps needed. OSS-research: no external cache library needed — plain localStorage Map is sufficient for <30 entries.

L1.recipe: Store first 3 words of query as prefix key → answer excerpt in localStorage alongside existing history. Simple prefix match on query start.

L2.recipe: Full LRU prefix cache (30 entries, 24h TTL). Prefix match shows 'Continuing from your earlier search' + excerpt + 'See full answer' link for deep queries.

L3.recipe: Server-side warm cache: scripts/build-ignis-cache-warmup.mjs pre-populates answers for the top 10 oracle queries (from oracle-query-insights.json) at build time as api/ignis-cache.json. ignis-answer-engine.js checks static cache first.
